questions.question: Which of the following Indian classical dances has originated from Andhra Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical Indian dance form that originated in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• This dance style is known for its graceful movements and strong narrative/dramatic character.
 
• It is named after the village of Kuchipudi in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh where it developed.
 
• Unlike other classical dances, Kuchipudi requires both dancing and singing by the performer.
 
• The dance form combines fast rhythms with fluid movements, creating a unique blend of control and abandon, strength and delicacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathakali** is from Kerala and is known for its elaborate costumes and makeup.
 
• **Odissi** hails from Odisha and is characterized by its fluid movements and sculpturesque poses.
 
• **Mohiniattam** is another classical dance from Kerala, known for its graceful and feminine movements.
 
• Each of these dance forms has its own unique history, style, and cultural significance, contributing to the rich tapestry of Indian classical dance.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the Badminton game and match length?

options.text: A match consists of the best of four games of 21 points.
A match consists of the best of three games of 21 points.
A match consists of the best of two games of 21 points.
A match consists of the best of five games of 21 points.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A match consists of the best of three games of 21 points**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A match in badminton consists of the best of three games of 21 points.
 
• The first player or pair to reach 21 points wins the game, provided there is a minimum lead of 2 points.
 
• If the score reaches 20-20, the game continues until one player or pair gains a 2-point lead (e.g., 22-20, 23-21).
 
• If the score reaches 29-29, the first player or pair to reach 30 points wins the game.
 
• The winner of a match is the first to win two games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Badminton is governed by the Badminton World Federation (BWF).
 
• The sport can be played in singles (one player per side) or doubles (two players per side).
 
• Badminton became an Olympic sport in 1992 at the Barcelona Games.
 
• The court dimensions for singles and doubles are different, with the doubles court being wider.
 
• Players must serve diagonally across the court to their opponent.
 
• The serve must be underhand and the shuttlecock must be hit below the server's waist.

questions.question: Jamshedi Navroz is a festival of _________ community.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parsi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jamshedi Navroz** is celebrated by the **Parsi** community.
 
• It marks the **Persian New Year** and is celebrated with great enthusiasm among Parsis.
 
• The festival falls on the **spring equinox**, around March 21st, and symbolizes rebirth, renewal, and rejuvenation.
 
• Parsis observe this day by cleaning their homes, wearing new clothes, and preparing special meals.
 
• The celebrations often include visiting the **fire temple** to offer prayers and seek blessings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Parsi community in India is primarily concentrated in **Mumbai** and **Gujarat**.
 
• Jamshedi Navroz is named after the legendary **King Jamshed** of Persia, who is credited with starting the Parsi calendar.
 
• The festival is also known as **Nowruz** in other parts of the world, including Iran and Central Asia.
 
• It is a day for Parsis to reflect on the past year and make new resolutions for the coming year.
 
• Traditional Parsi dishes such as **patra ni machhi** (steamed fish), **ravo** (sweet semolina pudding), and **falooda** (a sweet drink) are commonly prepared for the occasion.

questions.question: ________ Fundamental Duties were added in Part-IV-A of the Constitution under Article 51-A in the year 1976 through the 42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ten**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ten Fundamental Duties** were added to the Constitution of India in Part-IV-A under Article 51-A in the year 1976 through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment.
 
• These duties are intended to serve as a constant reminder to every citizen that while enjoying their rights, they also have obligations towards their country, society, and fellow citizens.
 
• The Fundamental Duties include respecting the national symbols, cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, and upholding and protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• Other duties encompass promoting harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood, protecting the environment, and striving towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 42nd Amendment Act, also known as the "Mini-Constitution," brought several other significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It attempted to reduce the power of the judiciary and increase the power of the central government.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were borrowed from the Constitution of the former Soviet Union and were intended to inculcate a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
• Initially, there were ten Fundamental Duties listed in Article 51-A, but an eleventh duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment in 2002.
 
• The eleventh duty is to provide opportunities for education to children between the ages of six and fourteen years.

questions.question: Which folk music of Jammu and Kashmir is sung in wedding ceremonies?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - Wanawun**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wanawun**

 
 
• Wanawun is a traditional folk music genre from **Jammu and Kashmir.**
 
• It is primarily sung during wedding ceremonies.
 
• The songs in Wanawun are often celebratory and filled with blessings for the newlyweds and their families.
 
• This type of music creates a joyful atmosphere, enhancing the overall wedding experience.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panihari**

 
 
• **Panihari is a type of folk music from Rajasthan.**
 
• It is traditionally sung by women while fetching water from wells or performing other daily chores.
 
• The songs often reflect the daily struggles, joys, and social issues faced by women in rural Rajasthan.
 
 
 
• **Alha**
 
 
• **Alha is a form of ballad singing from the Bundelkhand region in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• It involves narrating tales of bravery and heroism, often recounting the exploits of the legendary warriors Alha and Udal.
 
• Alha is not typically associated with wedding ceremonies but rather with festivals and gatherings.
 
 
 
• **Baul**
 
 
• **Baul is a form of mystic folk music from Bengal** (West Bengal in India and Bangladesh).
 
• Baul songs are characterized by their spiritual and philosophical themes, often focusing on love and devotion to God.
 
• This genre is more about individual spirituality and is not typically linked to wedding celebrations.

questions.question: Which from following unemployment scheme was extended by the government of India for a period of two years from July 2022 to June 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana** was extended by the Government of India for a period of two years from July 2022 to June 2024.
 
• This scheme is aimed at providing financial assistance to unemployed individuals who have lost their jobs due to various reasons.
 
• The scheme is implemented by the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) and provides relief to workers covered under the ESI scheme.
 
• Under this scheme, eligible unemployed individuals receive a cash benefit for up to 90 days during their unemployment period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana** was initially introduced in 2018 as a pilot scheme for two years.
 
• The scheme was extended for the first time from July 2020 to June 2022 before the latest extension.
 
• To avail the benefits, the unemployed individual must have been in insurable employment for a minimum of two years.
 
• The individual must have contributed to the ESI scheme for at least 78 days in each of the four contribution periods immediately preceding the unemployment.
 
• This scheme is part of the government’s efforts to provide social security to workers in the organized sector.
 
• The financial assistance provided under the scheme is equivalent to 50% of the average daily earnings of the individual.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about climate is INCORRECT?

options.text: ‘Monsoon’ type of climate is found mainly in south and southeast Asia.
India’s climate has characteristics of tropical as well as subtropical climates.
Coastal areas of India experience less contrasts in temperature conditions as compared to the interior of the country.
India experiences comparatively stronger winters as compared to central Asia.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India experiences comparatively stronger winters as compared to central Asia.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monsoon** type of climate is found mainly in south and southeast Asia.
 
• India's climate has characteristics of **tropical as well as subtropical climates**.
 
• Coastal areas of India experience **less contrasts in temperature conditions** as compared to the interior of the country.
 
• Central Asia experiences stronger winters compared to India due to its continental climate, which is characterized by more extreme seasonal temperature variations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's climate is significantly influenced by the **Himalayas and the Thar Desert**, which moderate the temperature and create monsoon conditions.
 
• The Himalayas act as a barrier to the frigid katabatic winds flowing down from Central Asia, keeping most of the Indian subcontinent warmer than most locations at similar latitudes.
 
• The **Thar Desert** plays a crucial role in attracting the moisture-laden southwest summer monsoon winds that bring most of India's rainfall during the year.
 
• India's diverse climate ranges from the **tropical climate** in the south to a more temperate climate in the north, and alpine in the higher Himalayan regions.

questions.question: The Yakshagana is the dance-drama primarily associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yakshagana** is a traditional dance-drama form that originated in the state of **Karnataka**.
 
• This art form combines dance, music, dialogue, costume, make-up, and stage techniques with a unique style and form.
 
• Yakshagana is traditionally presented from dusk to dawn and is associated with the coastal and Malnad regions of Karnataka.
 
• The themes of Yakshagana are usually drawn from Hindu epics such as the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word **Yakshagana** literally means the song (gana) of the Yaksha (nature spirits).
 
• It is believed to have evolved from pre-classical music and theatre during the Bhakti movement.
 
• Yakshagana performances are known for their vibrant costumes, elaborate headgear, and face painting, which are integral elements of the art form.
 
• There are different styles of Yakshagana, such as **Badagutittu** and **Tenkutittu**, which are distinguished by variations in dance, music, and costume.

questions.question: According to the Census of India, who are considered to be literates?

options.text: Person aged five and above, who can both read and write with understanding in any language
Person aged fifteen and above, who can both read and write with understanding in any language
Person aged eighteen and above, who can both read and write with understanding in any language
Person aged seven and above, who can both read and write with understanding in any language

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Person aged seven and above, who can both read and write with understanding in any language**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Census of India, a **literate** is a person aged **seven and above** who can both read and write with understanding in any language.
 
• This definition ensures that literacy is measured consistently across different regions and populations within the country.
 
• The literacy rate is an important indicator of educational attainment and socio-economic development.
 
• Efforts to improve literacy rates are crucial for the overall progress and empowerment of individuals and communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The literacy rate is calculated as the percentage of literates to the total population aged seven and above.
 
• Efforts by the government, non-governmental organizations, and international bodies have been ongoing to improve literacy rates in India.
 
• Literacy programs often focus on marginalized groups, including women, rural populations, and economically disadvantaged communities.
 
• Higher literacy rates contribute to better economic opportunities, improved health outcomes, and greater civic participation.

questions.question: What kind of technology is most frequently used to manage and digitise e-land records?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Geographic Information System (GIS)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Geographic Information System (GIS)** is the most frequently used technology to manage and digitize e-land records.
 
• GIS allows for the integration of various data types, which helps in creating detailed and accurate land records.
 
• This technology is essential for mapping, visualizing, and analyzing spatial data, which is crucial for land management and planning.
 
• GIS provides tools for querying, analyzing, and visualizing spatial data, making it easier for authorities to manage land records efficiently.
 
• It enhances transparency, reduces disputes related to land ownership, and improves the overall administration of land records.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Augmented Reality (AR)** and **Virtual Reality (VR)** are immersive technologies primarily used for interactive experiences and simulations, not for managing land records.
 
• **Blockchain** technology, while beneficial for ensuring the security and immutability of records, is not as widely used for the actual management and digitization of e-land records as GIS.
 
• The integration of GIS in land records management projects has shown significant improvement in the accuracy and accessibility of land records.
 
• Many countries and states have adopted GIS-based systems for better land management, indicating its effectiveness and reliability.

questions.question: According to Census of India 2011, which of the following states recorded the least population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sikkim** recorded the least population according to the Census of India 2011.
 
• The Census of India is conducted every ten years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• It is one of the most comprehensive sources of demographic data in India, covering various aspects such as population size, density, distribution, and various socio-economic indicators.
 
• Sikkim, being a small state in the northeastern part of India, has a significantly lower population compared to other states like Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Punjab.
 
• The low population can be attributed to its geographical terrain, limited land area, and other demographic factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Census of India 2011** was the 15th National Census since 1871 and marked the first time biometric information was collected.
 
• The total population of India according to the 2011 Census was over 1.21 billion.
 
• States with larger populations typically have more urban centers and industrial activities compared to smaller states like Sikkim.
 
• Understanding population distribution is crucial for planning and development, policy formulation, and resource allocation by the government.
 
• The next Census of India is scheduled to be conducted in 2021, which will provide updated demographic data.

questions.question: Certiorari comes under the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to constitutional remedies**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Certiorari** is a type of writ issued by a superior court to a lower court or tribunal either to transfer the matter to it or to quash the order of the lower court.
 
• This writ is issued to ensure that the jurisdiction of an inferior court or tribunal is properly exercised and that it does not exceed its jurisdiction.
 
• Certiorari comes under the **right to constitutional remedies**, which is enshrined in Article 32 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 32 provides the right to individuals to move the Supreme Court to seek justice when they feel that their rights are 'unduly deprived'.
 
• It ensures the protection of fundamental rights by allowing the Supreme Court to issue writs like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto, and Certiorari.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies** is often referred to as the 'heart and soul' of the Indian Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• It empowers citizens to stand up for the enforcement of their fundamental rights against any entity that violates them.
 
• This right is fundamental in ensuring the rule of law in the country.
 
• Other writs under Article 32 include:
 
 
• **Habeas Corpus** – to release a person who has been unlawfully detained.
 
• **Mandamus** – to direct a public authority to perform its duty.
 
• **Prohibition** – to prohibit a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction.
 
• **Quo-Warranto** – to challenge the legality of a person's claim to a public office.
 
 
 
• The right to constitutional remedies also extends to the High Courts under Article 226 of the Constitution.

questions.question: What is the main sense organ that virtual reality displays are aiming for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vision**__

__
 
• **Vision** is the primary sense organ targeted by virtual reality (VR) displays.
 
• VR displays are designed to create immersive visual experiences, making the user feel as if they are present in a virtual environment.
 
• High-resolution screens and advanced optics are used in VR headsets to enhance the visual experience.
 
• While other senses like touch and hearing are also important in VR, vision remains the main focus to achieve immersion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Virtual Reality (VR)** technology has applications in various fields such as gaming, education, healthcare, and training simulations.
 
• VR systems typically include a headset, motion controllers, and sometimes additional sensors to track the user's movements.
 
• Recent advancements in VR technology focus on improving visual fidelity, reducing latency, and increasing user comfort.
 
• Future developments in VR may also incorporate more advanced haptic feedback and sensory integration to enhance the overall immersive experience.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true?

i. The First Five-Year Plan was based on the PC Mahalanobis model.

ii. The First Five-Year Plan laid emphasis on agriculture development.

iii. The Five-Year planning model in India was borrowed from Russia.

• The **First Five-Year Plan** in India was launched in 1951 and primarily focused on the development of the agricultural sector.
 
• The **Five-Year planning model** in India was inspired by the planning model of the Soviet Union (Russia).
 
• The **PC Mahalanobis model** was actually used for the Second Five-Year Plan, not the first.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **First Five-Year Plan** was based on the Harrod-Domar model and emphasized on agricultural development to address the food crisis and inflationary pressures.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** introduced the PC Mahalanobis model which focused on industrialization and aimed at building a strong public sector.
 
• India adopted the Soviet-style planning model, which involved centralized and integrated national economic programs.

questions.question: In May 2023, the Supreme Court of India issued a set of directions to strengthen the POSH Act. To which of the following is this Act related?

options.text: Sexual harassment of women at workplace

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sexual harassment of women at workplace**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The POSH Act stands for the **Prevention of Sexual Harassment** at Workplace Act.
 
• It was enacted in **2013** to ensure a safe and secure working environment for women.
 
• The Act mandates the formation of an **Internal Complaints Committee (ICC)** at all workplaces with ten or more employees to address complaints of sexual harassment.
 
• The Act also outlines the **redressal mechanism** and the **penalties** for non-compliance by employers.
 
• In May 2023, the Supreme Court of India issued directions to **strengthen the implementation** of the POSH Act, emphasizing the need for active and effective ICCs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The POSH Act was formulated based on the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court in the **Vishaka case** in 1997.
 
• The Act covers not only traditional workplaces but also **extended workplaces** such as transportation provided by the employer, places visited by employees during the course of employment, etc.
 
• Employers are required to conduct **regular sensitization programs** and workshops to educate employees about the provisions of the Act and the importance of a harassment-free workplace.
 
• The Act also provides protection against **victimization** of the complainant and witnesses.
 
• Non-compliance with the POSH Act can lead to penalties, including fines and cancellation of business licenses.

questions.question: In which year did Hans Christian Oersted discover that a compass needle gets deflected when an electric current passes through a metallic wire placed nearby?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1820**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1820** is the year when Hans Christian Oersted discovered that a compass needle gets deflected by an electric current passing through a nearby metallic wire.
 
• Hans Christian Oersted was a Danish physicist and chemist who is known for this discovery, which showed a direct relationship between electricity and magnetism.
 
• This experiment laid the foundation for the field of electromagnetism, significantly influencing future scientific research and technological advancements.
 
• The discovery was a pivotal moment in the study of electromagnetism and led to the development of various technologies like electric motors and generators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hans Christian Oersted's discovery was accidental; he noticed the deflection of the compass needle while preparing for a lecture demonstration.
 
• This phenomenon demonstrated the fundamental connection between electric currents and magnetic fields, which was later formulated into Ampère's circuital law by André-Marie Ampère.
 
• Oersted's work was part of the broader 19th-century scientific movement that included contributions from other prominent scientists such as Michael Faraday and James Clerk Maxwell.
 
• The unit of magnetic field strength, the oersted (Oe), is named in his honor.
